beliefs.practice: Read the DOCUMENTDB_URI (MongoDB connection string) from an environment variable at runtime and never commit connection strings or keys to source control or logs; in production fetch secrets from Azure Key Vault.

Use a single, long-lived pymongo.MongoClient per process (do not recreate per request) and configure connection pooling (set maxPoolSize appropriate to concurrency), e.g. MongoClient(DOCUMENTDB_URI, maxPoolSize=100, appname='interest-rate-scenario-modeler').

Enable TLS/SSL for all client connections and validate server certificates (do not set tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true); ensure driver connection string includes tls=true and, when required, provide the CA bundle.
Create an application-scoped least-privilege database user for sample_banking_08 with only the roles/privileges required (read or readWrite on the single DB) rather than using admin/root credentials.
Make seed and write operations idempotent (use upsert with a stable client-generated id) so retries don’t create duplicate positions.

Create and maintain a compound index on the fields used by the aggregation/grouping and filters, e.g. {maturity_bucket: 1, rate_type: 1, trade_date: -1} (include exposure in the index if queries can be covered).

If you compute maturity buckets frequently, either store a precomputed maturity_bucket field at write time or ensure an index exists on the computed fields used by $bucket/$group to avoid full-collection scans.
Place selective $match stages as early as possible in the aggregation pipeline and project only required fields with $project to minimize data scanned and RU/IO consumption.

Validate and tune aggregation pipelines using explain() / the provider's query plan tools before running workloads in production; verify the pipeline uses the intended index with the DocumentDB MCP or explain output.

Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network/MongoNetworkError exceptions (and limit total retries); treat potentially non-idempotent writes specially or use upsert with a stable id.
Tune client-side timeouts to detect failures quickly: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g. 5000 ms) and socketTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS according to application latency tolerance.

When using the MongoDB vector features, store embeddings consistently (fixed dimension, float32), normalize when using cosine, and create a vector index (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) on the embedding field with tuned params (e.g., M=16, efConstruction=200, efSearch=64) appropriate for recall/latency tradeoffs.
Limit aggregation result sizes with $limit or pagination rather than returning unbounded result sets; use server-side cursors and iterate with reasonable batchSize to control memory and RU usage.

Create schema validation rules on the collection (validator JSON Schema) to enforce required fields like maturity_date, rate_type, exposure and embedding dimension at insert/update to avoid garbage data.

Programmatically check for existing indexes before creating new ones (idempotent index creation) and keep index-creation in migration/seed scripts rather than creating ad-hoc at runtime for predictability.
Monitor RU/throughput, index usage, and slow queries; set alerts for RU throttling (429) and sudden RU spikes and use explain() or profiler to identify and fix heavy aggregation stages.

Provision throughput appropriate to the expected load (use autoscale/elastic scale when traffic varies) to avoid throttling during large aggregation runs, and test RU usage of the aggregation under realistic data volumes.

Restrict network access to the cluster using firewall IP rules, VNet / private endpoints, or the provider's network security features; do not expose the database to the public internet without controls.

Keep embeddings and other high-cardinality fields out of frequently-updated documents where possible (or store them in a separate collection) to avoid expensive index updates and large document transfers during aggregation.
Log only operational metadata (timings, RU consumed, query ids) from aggregation runs; never log secrets or full documents in production logs to avoid data leakage.
